Perusal of invoice No.435 shows that six kind of spices were delivered to the defendants and their total price including GST was Rs.5,34,245/-.
Vide invoice No.612, only two kinds of spices were delivered and their total price including GST is only Rs.1,53,400/-.
Had the goods of invoice No.435 been of defective quality, the same kind and number of goods of same price goods would have been delivered to them vide invoice No.612.
But it is not so.
The goods delivered vide invoice No.612 were one third in quantity as well as in price to the goods described in invoice No.435.

As per Section 41 of the Sales of Goods Act, 1930, when the goods are delivered to the buyer which he has not previously examined, he has right to examine them before accepting, for the purpose of ascertaining whether they were in conformity with the contract or not.
As per Section 42 of the Act, the buyer is deemed to have accepted the goods in three circumstance.
First is when he intimates the seller that he had accepted the goods.
Second is that he does any act in relation to the goods which is inconsistent with the ownership of the seller.
The third circumstance is that he retains the goods without intimating to the seller that he has rejected them.
UMED SINGH M/S Ashwmegh Spices Pvt. Ltd vs M/S Sana Food Products

This issue is decided in favour of plaintiff and against all defendants.
Issue No.2 16.
It is mentioned in invoices that interest at the rate of 18% per annum would be charged if payment was not made within ten days.

But that rate is not only excessive but penal also and so interest at the rate of 9% per annum is granted from the date of last delivery transaction i.e.
09.11.2017 till realization with cost.
Issue No.3 17.

In view of above discussion, the suit is decreed in the sum of Rs.6,69,753/- and defendants are jointly and severally liable to pay the said amount to the plaintiff with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of last delivery transaction i.e. 09.11.2017 till realization with cost.

After taking of so clear position, it is not appropriate for them to take u-turn and take a new stand at the stage of final arguments.
As per Section 34 of Indian Evidence Act, the ledger account is relevant but that in itself is not sufficient to decide the case against opposite party.
The present case does not pertain to the transactions with the defendants at Meerut address.
In view of above explanation, the plaintiff is justified not to show entry of Rs.2,27,560/- in ledger account statement for the deliveries made to the defendant at Rishikesh, Uttrakhand address because the said payment has been shown in the account statement for the deliveries made to defendants at their Meerut address.
As per Section 41 of the Sales of Goods Act, 1930, when the goods are delivered to the buyer which he has not previously examined, he has right to examine them before accepting, for the purpose of ascertaining whether they were in conformity with the contract or not.
As per Section 42 of the Act, the buyer is deemed to have accepted the goods in three circumstance.
First is when he intimates the seller that he had accepted the goods.
Second is that he does any act in relation to the goods which is inconsistent with the ownership of the seller.
UMED SINGH M/S Ashwmegh Spices Pvt. Ltd vs M/S Sana Food Products

But that rate is not only excessive but penal also and so interest at the rate of 9% per annum is granted from the date of last delivery transaction i.e.
09.11.2017 till realization with cost.
